title: Fairness and Bias in Algorithmic Hiring: A Multidisciplinary Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Survey of literature on algorithmic hiring, reviewing biases arising from occupational segregation, wage gaps, stereotype violations, and gendered language, evaluated through fairness metrics like Disparate Impact and True Positive Rate Difference.

Survey of literature on algorithmic hiring, examining direct discrimination, disparities introduced by background checks, and disparate performance of language and vision models across racial and ethnic groups.
Survey of literature discussing how job ad delivery optimization and automated evaluations can skew against or filter out older job applicants.

Survey of literature highlighting accessibility issues, ableist norms, and the mismeasurement of candidates with speech or sight impairments in automated hiring tools such as asynchronous video interviews.
Survey of literature detailing biases stemming from elitism (favoring prestigious institutions), social network topologies, and geographic factors like commute times and residential segregation.
